title: Define the HumbleStudio Board product contract
summary: Starting with gestures or drawing primitives would bake storage, identity, source linkage and editing semantics into UI code before the product knows what a Board object means. Define a versioned Board domain and ADR covering document ownership, object kinds, coordinate system, stable identity, source references, proposal state and non-goals.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned Board ADR defines product purpose, primary user workflows, document ownership and explicit non-goals for the first release.
The domain defines Board, Page, Layer, Object, Transform, Bounds, SourceReference and ObjectKind without importing SwiftUI, AppKit or web types.
Object kinds distinguish at least freeform shape/text/image, diagram node/edge, screen artboard and repository artifact reference.
The coordinate system, units, z-order, grouping, stable identity, deletion and unknown-future-object behavior are documented.
The contract states that imported StudioNativeDocument remains read-only and Board changes remain proposals until a later apply workflow.
A staged roadmap maps each accepted Board capability to HS tickets and avoids claiming collaboration or source-code editing in MVP.
Ticket, repo-contract and diff validation pass.

evidence.note: The current design contract models imported tokens, components, views and navigation only.
The native workspace is an inspection and review surface.
Future authoring is explicitly read-only and proposal-first.
Write-back and source mutation are explicitly not implemented.

trigger.source_ref: HumbleStudio Board architecture finding HS-BAR-001, requested by Jan.

agent_notes: Board changes must remain proposal-first and must not mutate source truth unless a future separately accepted apply contract permits it.
Do not broaden this slice into real-time collaboration, arbitrary source rewrite or a provider-specific AI architecture.
Rejected alternative: Build an infinite canvas first and infer the model later — UI state would become the accidental persistence and collaboration contract.
